sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What musical term is used to describe the speed or pace of a piece of music or a dance?
In Indian classical dance, what is the primary purpose of using 'Mudras' (hand gestures)?
options: B) To keep the hands warm
C) To express emotions and narrate stories
D) To block the stage lights
questions.answer: C) To express emotions and narrate stories

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a traditional folk dance from Gujarat that involves moving in a circle?
When we turn everyday activities, like sweeping or washing, into a dance routine, what are we doing?
What creates the basic 'rhythm' in a piece of music?
options: B) A repeated pattern of beats and pauses
C) Playing all instruments at once
questions.answer: B) A repeated pattern of beats and pauses

questions.question_text: Which of these instruments produces sound by striking a stretched skin or membrane?
How can a dancer best show the emotion of anger without using any spoken words?
options: A) By smiling and waving gently
B) By stamping feet heavily and narrowing the eyes
C) By skipping lightly on toes
D) By yawning and lying down
questions.answer: B) By stamping feet heavily and narrowing the eyes

questions.question_text: In a choir, what happens when many people 'Sing and Play' together properly?
options: A) They follow the same rhythm and melody to sound harmonious
B) Everyone sings a different song loudly
D) The instruments are hidden away
questions.answer: A) They follow the same rhythm and melody to sound harmonious

questions.question_text: What does a 'building block' refer to in the creation of music?
options: A) A heavy brick used to build a stage
B) A short musical phrase or beat pattern used to build a song
C) A type of wooden drumstick
D) The curtain of the theatre
questions.answer: B) A short musical phrase or beat pattern used to build a song

questions.question_text: When dancing to a fast, highly energetic beat, which movements are most appropriate?
options: B) Quick jumping, fast spins, and sharp hand gestures
D) Closing the eyes and breathing deeply
questions.answer: B) Quick jumping, fast spins, and sharp hand gestures

questions.question_text: How do different sounds in our environment give us ideas and inspiration to create music? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Everyday sounds, like rain falling or birds chirping, give us ideas for rhythms and melodies. We can mimic these natural sounds using musical instruments to create unique songs.

questions.question_text: Explain how you can turn a simple everyday activity, like brushing your teeth, into a dance movement. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: You can turn it into a dance by exaggerating your arm motions, adding a rhythmic bounce to your steps, and doing it playfully in time with upbeat music.

questions.question_text: Why is teamwork and coordination important when performing a group dance with your classmates? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Teamwork ensures everyone stays in sync with the rhythm and each other. It prevents collisions on stage and makes the final performance look beautiful and fully united.

questions.question_text: Describe the difference between a high-pitched sound and a low-pitched sound using two musical instruments as examples. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A flute makes a sharp, high-pitched whistling sound like a bird, while a large bass drum produces a deep, low-pitched booming sound like heavy thunder.

questions.question_text: How can a dancer effectively express the feeling of sadness during a solo stage performance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A dancer can show sadness by using slow, heavy movements, dropping their shoulders, looking downward, and keeping a gentle, sorrowful expression on their face.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are creating a dance that tells the story of a seed growing into a tall tree. Describe the sequence of your body movements from start to finish. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I would start by curling tightly on the floor to represent a tiny seed. Slowly, as the music softens, I would unfold my limbs and rise upward. Finally, I would stand tall on my toes, swaying my arms widely to mimic branches blowing in the wind.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are part of a school orchestra playing a piece of music about a thunderstorm. Describe the instruments used and the sounds they make to create the storm. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The large bass drums would crash loudly to sound like booming thunder, while the violins would play fast, high, and scratchy notes to mimic fierce, howling winds. We would gently shake the tambourines at the end to sound like soft, fading raindrops.

questions.question_text: Describe how you would choreograph a short folk dance that celebrates the harvest season in your nation, focusing on rhythm and facial expressions. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would choreograph a lively and joyful dance set to a fast, upbeat drum rhythm. The dancers would wear bright costumes and form a large, moving circle. The steps would include energetic jumps and wide arm swings to mimic cutting crops, with huge, happy smiles to express gratitude for a plentiful harvest.

questions.question_text: How would you use two everyday objects found in your classroom to create a musical rhythm for a song? Describe the specific actions and the sounds they produce. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would use two wooden rulers and a hollow plastic dustbin to create a beat. First, I would tap the rulers together sharply to make a high, clicking sound. Then, I would strike the bottom of the inverted dustbin to create a deep, hollow thump. Alternating these actions would build a catchy rhythm.
